    🎭 Curtain
    Nov 10, 2026 This Week's Topics
    INews in Review
    Week Ending Oct 31
    Final days before the midterms: Democrats projected to win a 230–205 House and a narrow Senate majority. Covers redistricting, Trump-backed voter-fraud claims, DOJ actions, tight Senate and governor races, and fears of interference with vote counting and certification.
    Week Ending Nov 7
    A Blue Tidal Wave ! Election week fallout and transition: post-midterm analysis, balance-of-power projections, and the opening moves of the new political landscape heading into the lame-duck session.
    IIOpening Round — Your Reactions
    An open invitation to every member of the group: share your feelings and reactions to this week's election. What surprised you? What concerned you? What gave you hope? All voices welcome.
    The Great Exhale
    The collective breath released after a tense election season: what it feels like when the ballots are counted and the country begins to process what just happened.
    IIIPolitics and the Pendulum
    Voters do swing power between parties — but policy doesn't simply reverse. A century of data shows the top tax rate has stayed in a 28–40% band under both parties, and major programs tend to persist regardless of who governs.
    IVWithin Reach
    A Democratic Congress starting in January 2027 could still check the Trump administration without controlling the White House — through subpoenas, contempt, spending-bill riders, Senate confirmation holds, and impeachment, while noting where a presidential signature or veto override would still be required.
    VHistorical Context of Talarico's Speech
    Compares Lincoln's 1865 Second Inaugural and Talarico's 2026 election-night speech and how each uses the Bible. Lincoln let brief scripture allusions carry meaning; Talarico names, retells, and explains biblical stories for an audience with thinner biblical knowledge.
    VIMagic Wand Retrospective
    Revisits BOLLI's "Magic Wand Challenge" — what Democrats would do with full power to undo Trump-era damage — in light of the November 2026 midterms. Democrats won Congress but not the White House, leaving the key policy questions from that exercise still open.
    In The Twilight of DJT
    Future Sessions
    🔖 On the Table
    AI
    AI Puts the Billable Hour on Trial
    Nearly 90% of U.K. and Irish legal professionals now use AI, which lets firms take on more work while cutting administrative overhead. The traditional hourly billing model is under serious strain — and with it, how junior lawyers are trained.
    John Maynard Keynes Speaks Through an AI Bot
    An AI-simulated Keynes weighs in on technological unemployment, the 15-hour work week he predicted, and whether today's economy vindicates or confounds his vision.
    Legal Engineer
    As AI reshapes legal work, a new hybrid role is emerging — the legal engineer — who combines law, technology, and process design to build the systems that tomorrow's law firms will run on.
    The Fifties Revisited
    The Fifties and Now
    Drawing on Halberstam's The Fifties, this visualization tracks parallels between the late 1940s and October 2026 — party infighting, an ongoing war, cratering trust in government, and what the polling of then and now reveals.
    Selling the President — 1952
    How Eisenhower's 1952 campaign became the first to use television advertising to sell a presidential candidate like a consumer product — and what it set in motion for every election since.
    The Man from Independence and DJT From Queens
    A side-by-side comparison of Truman and Trump across ten measures — wealth, education, military service, corruption, and legacy — drawing on Halberstam's portrait and Trump's public record.
    Present Current Events
    Balance of Power
    A real-time look at the post-election balance of power in Washington — House and Senate seat counts, key committee control, and what the new alignment means for the legislative agenda ahead.
